Test rows of another view in a window around the encounter

Source: R/cohort_criteria.R
view_rows.Rd

A test for criterion(): rows of view for the same patient whose date_col falls within window days of the encounter date are judged by condition. Which rows are judged is pick:

Usage

view_rows(view, date_col, window, pick, condition, mrn_col = "mrn")

Arguments

view

Character. A view in the same database, optionally schema-qualified.

date_col

Character. The view's date or timestamp column. Timestamps are cast to dates.

window

Integer vector of length two: first and last day relative to the encounter date, inclusive. c(-30, 0) is the 30 days before, and the day of, surgery.

pick

"any", "all" or "nearest".

condition

Character. A SQL boolean expression over the view's columns, written by the study programmer. Every column it names must exist in the view.

mrn_col

Character. The view's patient identifier column.

Value

An object of class cohort_test.

Details

  • "any": met if any row meets the condition.

  • "all": met if every row meets it.

  • "nearest": the row or rows nearest the encounter date must agree, and their verdict is the test's.

The test is undetermined when there is no row in the window, when a row's condition is unknown and the verdict depends on it, or when rows tied for nearest disagree. None of date_col, window or pick has a default: they are the study's choices.

Windows are whole days on dates. "Within 72 hours before surgery" written as c(-3, 0) is wider than 72 hours, and the provenance records the day window used.

See also

criterion(), master_row(), any_of()

Examples

view_rows("echo_measure", date_col = "measured_on", window = c(-30, 0),
          pick = "nearest", condition = "lvef <= 25")
#> $type
#> [1] "view"
#> 
#> $view
#> [1] "echo_measure"
#> 
#> $date_col
#> [1] "measured_on"
#> 
#> $window
#> [1] -30   0
#> 
#> $pick
#> [1] "nearest"
#> 
#> $condition
#> [1] "lvef <= 25"
#> 
#> $mrn_col
#> [1] "mrn"
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "cohort_test"
